name: imageblock-array-slices-the-copy-did-not-name-are-untouched
no_effect: The tile copy names another slice, so the observed slice keeps its authored fill.
rationale: The other half of imageblock-tile-lands-on-the-addressed-array-slice: the copy names slice 2, so slice 0 must still hold the (-1, -2, -3, -4) fill, which no cell can produce. Without this the evidence says a correct tile arrived somewhere and not that it arrived only where it was addressed -- a lowering that dropped the slice operand and wrote every layer, or that wrote layer 0 as well, passes the first case and fails this one.

name: imageblock-scalar-tile-on-a-second-array-slice
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d_array.i16.f16 (11 case-less corpus sources), over the same tile as imageblock-tile-lands-on-the-addressed-array-slice. This plane is one channel where that one is four and sits at byte 8 of the cell, and it goes to a different slice of a different array texture, so a lowering that took the slice index from the wrong operand -- the level sits beside it in the AIR call -- cannot satisfy both cases. The weight is x + 32 * y, distinct across all 1024 cells.

name: imageblock-tile-lands-on-the-addressed-array-slice
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d_array.i16.v4f16 (17 case-less corpus sources). A 32x32 threadgroup stages a colour of (x, y, x / 2, y / 4) into its own imageblock cell and thread (0, 0) copies the whole tile to array slice 2 of a three-slice texture. The four channels scale differently, so a copy that transposed the tile or swizzled the texel lands a quadruple that exists nowhere in it. The 16-byte cell puts 1024 of them at exactly the 16384 bytes of threadgroup memory Vulkan guarantees, which is where this translator stops allocating cells, so running the case is what makes that budget measured rather than chosen.

name: colorize-uint-trace-single-cross
rationale: One thread at gid (0,0) reads input texel (0,0) as the trace position (1,1). The cross half-extent is int(max(4/2, 4/2) * 0.1) = 0, so each of the two write loops runs from -1 through 1 and stops: exactly three horizontal and three vertical stores, all inside the 4x4 output. A single thread also means no two invocations write the same texel, so the whole attachment is exactly determined.

name: linked-gather-vector-matrix-float-k439-second-matrix-tg-reduction
rationale: Reaching variant of 3c4e0438 (linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-float), whose zero kernel-info word and params leave the kernel no K and no rows. The constants select an Apple device (constant 127 bit 10) whose threadgroup shape comes from the kernel-info word: 8 simdgroups, 32 threads along K and 8 rows (grid and threadgroup 32x8x1); the gather (constant 124 bit 13, every threadgroup id kept), 4-wide B loads, a K tile of 2, the partial reduction step, the K tail (not divisible by 4), the alpha multiply, the y edge check, the threadgroup-memory reduction (no simd reduction: 1024 bytes, one float per thread) and the linked destination callback. N = 8 rows of K = 439: the two whole steps (numDeviceReductionsDownTileK 2) cover elements 0 to 255, the partial steps 2 and 3 (numDeviceReductions 4) elements 256 to 435 (K4 = 436: lanes 0 to 12 of step 3), and thread 0 of each row the tail 436 to 438. P = 1 and indices[0] = 1, so the kernel reads the second of two float A matrices (AMatrixBytes = 8 rows of 440 elements): A_e[n][k] = (5k + 3n + floor(kn/4) + 2e) mod 7 - 3, so expert 0 would give other sums; B[k] = (3k + floor(k/5)) mod 5 - 1 (float, BRowBytes one element). Thread (0, n) writes alpha * D[n] (alpha 0.5) through the callback at coordinate n: table entry 1's 8 floats, each written once. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 9 and every partial sum an integer below 2^12, exact in float in any order, and the alpha product is exact. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the step counts, K4 and the constant thread counts bound the reduction loops, and the tree halves 32 to 1.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-float
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The zero kernel-info word sets the reduction tile, SIMD count, K extent, postfix-link flag, and fusion modes to zero. With zero matrix parameters, the sole invocation has no reduction or destination work and leaves the bounded poisoned destination unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: vertex-float2-varying-passthrough
rationale: Three authored float4 positions form a full-coverage triangle and constant float2 attributes traverse the declared varying; the typed varying observer captures both lanes over the complete two-by-two target.

name: vertex-position-passthrough
rationale: Three authored float4 clip-space attributes form a full-coverage triangle; the typed position observer captures the passthrough position interface over the complete two-by-two target.

name: srgb-decode-both-arms-and-the-alpha-exponent
rationale: A one-texel source makes the sampled half4 independent of the harness-fixed varying. Red zero takes the linear arm and stays zero; green one takes the transfer arm, where (1 + 0.055) * (1 / 1.055) is exactly one in float32 so air.fast_powr.f32 must return exactly one; alpha one pins air.powr.f16 at the same fixed point. The captured texel is half4(0, 1, 0, 1), so a lowering that swaps the two arms, drops either powr, or evaluates it at the wrong base changes the bytes.

name: depthwise-conv3d-cfirst-2x2x2-writes-every-channel
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-parameters case of this entry, whose zero destination size fails every thread's bounds check. User constant 124 = 0: the parameter path (smallParamsFC 0), channel axis 0, no channel multiplier; constant 112 = 0 (padding mode 0). dstSize = (W, H, D, C) = (3, 2, 2, 4), srcSize = (4, 3, 3, 4), a 2x2x2 kernel, unit strides and dilations, zero offsets. One threadgroup of 4x3x4 threads, gid = (c, x, d * H + y): all 48 pass the bounds checks, walk the 8 taps of their window, and write coordinate (c, x, y, d) through the linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec, table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component), so words 0 to 3 (c) are written and words 4 to 7 keep the 0xab fill. The retained modules of the source callbacks the case links return constants (prefixPrimary_f 1.0, prefixSecondary_f 0.0; the only retained modules of those functions), so every tap's product is 0.0 and every sum exactly +0.0 in any order; every writer of a word stores that same value, so the observed words do not depend on write order. The variant observes the loops, the bounds checks and the written coordinates, not data-dependent arithmetic. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the three tap loops run kernelSizes = 2 times each.

name: depthwise-conv3d-cfirst-zero-parameters

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nineteen-threadgroup-primary

The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: nan-model-float-denormals-per-operation
rationale: Which float operations read a denormal operand as a zero of its sign, and which flush a denormal result, in Metal's compile without fast math. Lane i reads (a, b, c) and writes 48 words: a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b, fma(a, b, c), a * b + c, -a, 0 - a, fabs(a), copysign(a, b), a < b and a == b as 0 or 1; floor, ceil, trunc, round, rint, fract, sign, saturate, sqrt, rsqrt, log2, log, sin, tan, atan, asin, sinh, tanh, asinh, atanh of a; pow(a, b), powr(a, b), fmod(a, b), ldexp(a, 4), dot(float2(a, b), float2(b, c)), length(float2(a, b)), mix(a, b, c), step(a, b), smoothstep(a, b, c), atan2(a, b), fmin(a, b), (a * b) * c, (a / b) * c, a < b ? a : b, -(a * b), and fabs(a - b). Lanes: every pair (a, b) of +-2^-149, 3 * 2^-149, 2^-127, both largest denormals, +-2^-126, +-1, 0.5, 3, 2^-100, 2^-30, 2^-120, and 2^10, with c from the same set: denormal operands of each sign, and normal pairs whose product, quotient, or difference is a denormal. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: empty-asm-in-a-loop-body-runs-every-iteration
rationale: The loop body begins with `asm volatile("")`, the one inline assembly MSL accepts, which compiles to a call of `asm sideeffect "", ""` and which the translator drops at decode. The trip count is n = 6 from a buffer, so no compiler can fold it. Each of the 4 threads stores all six partial sums of i ^ t to words 8 + 8t + i, its sum to word 2t and its iteration count to word 2t + 1; the other words keep the 0xab fill. Every word is observed, so a loop shortened or removed once the barrier is gone shows as a mismatch.

name: empty-asm-in-an-inlined-helper
rationale: `asm volatile("")` in a noinline helper the kernel calls: the call of `asm sideeffect "", ""` sits in the helper's body, which the translator inlines after decode dropped the call. Each of the 4 threads writes 3t + 1, the helper's answer, to word t.

name: linked-single-radix7-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-7 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: land-a-device-address-field-atomic
rationale: An integer compare-exchange on a FLOAT device slot, through a device pointer parked in a local struct field and read back by an out-of-line helper. The integer-atomic-over-a-float-slot is what selects the physical-address model -- Logical SPIR-V cannot retype a logical pointer -- so the whole device-address path runs: the field store records the pointer as a 64-bit address, the helper reads it back, and the atomic lands on an OpConvertUToPtr PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer. Twelve corpus sources translate through that path and none had an authored case. Even threads' slots start at 0.0f (zero bits), so their exchange succeeds and overwrites the float with the integer i+100; odd threads' start at 3.5f, so theirs fails and leaves the slot alone. This case compares the SLOT buffer afterwards, so it pins WHERE the write landed: even slots must hold the integer i+100 and odd ones must still hold 3.5f.

name: observe-a-device-address-field-atomic
rationale: An integer compare-exchange on a FLOAT device slot, through a device pointer parked in a local struct field and read back by an out-of-line helper. The integer-atomic-over-a-float-slot is what selects the physical-address model -- Logical SPIR-V cannot retype a logical pointer -- so the whole device-address path runs: the field store records the pointer as a 64-bit address, the helper reads it back, and the atomic lands on an OpConvertUToPtr PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer. Twelve corpus sources translate through that path and none had an authored case. Even threads' slots start at 0.0f (zero bits), so their exchange succeeds and overwrites the float with the integer i+100; odd threads' start at 3.5f, so theirs fails and leaves the slot alone. This case compares what each thread OBSERVED, so it pins the value the atomic read back at the address it computed.

name: nan-model-vector-float-half-conversions-of-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_convert_fast (nan_convert's program under the default fast math, the flagged state of the conversions): lane i reads a float4 a and a half4 h and writes half4(a) (two words), half(a.x) | half(a.y) << 16 (the scalar fptrunc), float(h.x) (the scalar fpext), and float4(h) (four words). Values: every float NaN kind (quiet and signaling of either sign, payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3fe000, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff), the narrowing's range and rounding edges (+-65504, 65519.996, +-65520, 2^-24, 2^-25, 3 * 2^-26, 2^-14, a float denormal, 1e30) and controls; every half NaN kind (payloads 0, 1, 2, 0xaa, 0x155, 0x1fe, 0x1ff), the infinities, +-65504, subnormals and controls; each value in every vector lane. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fifteen-threadgroup-primary

name: convolution-weight-gradient-1x1-one-tile-channel-and-spatial-remainders
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-output-channel case of this entry. User constant 124 = 0x1D028: tile sizes K = C = 32 and unroll 8 (the shape the kernel's fixed 8-step inner loop and its 8-lane by 16-row thread split assume), data and weight formats 0. Parameters: C = 20 input and K = 10 output channels in one group, a 1x1 kernel with unit stride and dilation and no offset, batch 2, data and gradient 3x2, and two iterations of the spatial loop (16 slots for 12 positions; magic divisors 6 and 3 split a position into (n, y, x), checked exact for every index below 65536). One threadgroup of 128 threads is the whole dispatch for this problem (one kernel tap, one channel tile each way, 2048 bytes of threadgroup memory). Each iteration loads data (prefixPrimary_f) and gradient (prefixTertiary_f) values for 8 positions into threadgroup memory behind bounds checks, with zero for positions of batch 2 and channels at or past C or K, synchronizes, and accumulates 8 float4 products per thread; after the loop each thread writes its 4 output channels for input channel tid/8 and, when below C, tid/8 + 16, each behind a k < K check. The retained prefixPrimary_f module returns 1.0 and prefixTertiary_f 0.0 (their only retained modules here), so every product is +0.0 and every sum exactly +0.0 in any order. The linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec, table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component) receives coordinate (k, c, 0, 0), so words 0 to 9 are written, every writer storing the same +0.0 so the words do not depend on write order, and words 10 and 11 keep the 0xab fill. The variant observes the tiling, the bounds checks, the barriers and the write coverage, not data-dependent arithmetic. Loops are bounded: the spatial loop runs the parameter's 2 iterations and the inner loop a fixed 8.

name: sum-a-constant-weight-run-walked-by-a-nested-loop
rationale:
A `constant`-space induction pointer walked by a NESTED loop, so the pointer is a CYCLE of phis rather than a single self-recursive one -- the shape `raw_only_induction_phi` refused until this commit.

The emitter models a buffer raw when it cannot type the walk, and then the induction pointer has no SPIR-V pointer value: the descriptor root and the byte offset live only in `raw_offsets`, and `emit_raw_pointer_phi` re-materializes them as a word index. It only claimed the phi when every arm was already raw under the root or was a forward GEP off the phi ITSELF. Here the outer loop's carried pointer is advanced by the INNER loop: its backedge arm is a GEP off the inner header's phi, whose own entry arm is the outer phi. No arm of either phi is a GEP off that phi, so both fell to `Private` zero placeholders -- and a phi whose arms are a placeholder and a real `StorageBuffer` pointer has no common type, which is why the module does not merely read zeros here but fails to construct at all (`owned OpPhi incoming type does not match`, then `non-spillable-demote` in the state machine). Walking the cycle admits every member together.

The `.ll` is hand-written and the `.metal` is the same computation in a different spelling, which is what the fixture pair allows: Metal runs the `.metal` and the translator reads the `.ll`. The Metal front end cannot emit this shape from the `.metal` -- the inner trip count is the constant 3, so it rewrites the outer backedge as a single `gep %outer, 3`, which is a GEP off the outer phi and exactly the one-phi shape the old code already handled. Both spellings were simulated independently over all eight threads before authoring and Metal's answer is the sequence derived from the `.metal` one.

The answer discriminates the walk exactly. `weights[k].x` is `k + 1` for the twelve `float4`s the two loops cover (4 x 3), so the sum is 78, an integer exact in binary32, and every partial sum is an integer under 78 -- no rounding enters the answer and the accumulation order cannot matter. `acc` starts at `float(gid)`, so the eight lanes answer 78..85 and a broadcast or a lane mix-up is visible. A pointer that never advanced would answer `gid + 12`; one that advanced by 3 float4s per LOAD instead of per iteration would run off the end; one that read `.y`, `.z` or `.w` would answer a large negative, since the other three components are -100-k, -200-k and -300-k. The output buffer is pre-filled with -1.0, so a lane that is not written at all is visible too.

Both loops are bounded in the AIR itself by constant trip counts (3 and 4) with no input or function constant involved, hence `authored_bounded`. Each thread writes only its own slot, so nothing races.

name: vertex-input-of-a-dynamic-stride-layout-of-an-executed-draw-template
rationale: The render template of executed draws whose vertex buffer the host binds at attribute strides, run as its own case: a rasterization-disabled vertex function whose vertex input 0, a uint, has a layout of MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic, so the fetch reads the stride the buffer is bound with; both executors bind its data (element i = 0x7000 + 5 * i, at the oracle's slot 30) with the stride form at stride 4. A point draw of 8 vertices, one instance: vertex v writes out[v] = (0x7000 + 5 * v, v).

name: erode-a-four-voxel-luma-line-against-its-two-neighbours
rationale: The kernel samples a texture3d at the voxel centre and at +/-1 in x with a pixel-coordinate nearest clamp-to-edge sampler, multiplies the three red channels and broadcasts the product. Powers of two make every product exact in half, and the clamped ends repeat their edge voxel, so the four written voxels pin the offset, the clamp and the channel selection at once.

name: gemm-i2i8-a18-zero-shape
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output. The only multiply is a 16x16x16 int8 simdgroup matrix product, which needs Apple GPU family 10; it sits in the K loop, and every configuration that writes output runs it. Neither the M3 Max nor the M4 has family 10 (the Metal reference gap of the signed-off conv2d cases), so no computing variant can be qualified.
rationale: One thread (a 1x1 grid) with zero M/N/K matrix parameters selects the no-work tile extent. Function constant 115 (fc0) is 0x10100: kNumMSIMD and kKSplits decode to 1 and every other field is 0 (the per-simdgroup tile counts, kNumNSIMD, the barrier iterations, and every feature flag, so the optional atomic and threadgroup bindings stay disabled). Every divisor on the path is nonzero: K by kKSplits times 64 (64), and the simdgroup index and its K-split quotient by kKSplits and kNumMSIMD (1); every shift amount is a constant. No loop iterates and nothing is written: all ABI resources and the exact postfix linkage are present, and the observed D bytes remain unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.
